questions.q: Define system software and give two examples with their specific functions in a computer system.
questions.a: System software is a set of programs that directly manages computer hardware and provides a platform for other software. Examples: (1) Operating System (e.g., Windows, Linux) — manages CPU scheduling, memory allocation, file systems, and provides user interface; (2) Device Driver (e.g., printer driver) — translates OS commands into device-specific signals. A wrong answer (e.g., "MS Word is system software") reveals the student confuses user-facing programs with hardware-management programs, indicating they haven't grasped the hardware-interface criterion.

questions.q: Explain why a computer cannot function without system software but can function without application software. Use the terms "hardware," "interface," and "user tasks" in your explanation.
questions.a: System software provides the essential interface between hardware and all other software; without it, the CPU cannot be scheduled, memory cannot be allocated, and devices cannot be controlled — so no program (including application software) can execute. Application software performs specific user tasks (typing, browsing) but relies on system software for hardware access. A computer with only an OS (no Word, no browser) can still boot, run commands, and manage files — it functions as a computer. A wrong answer (e.g., "both are equally necessary") reveals the student doesn't understand the hierarchical dependency: system software is the prerequisite layer.

questions.q: Classify each of the following as System Software (SS), Application Software (AS), or Programming Tool (PT): Ubuntu, MS Word, Printer Driver, Photoshop, Python Interpreter, Disk Defragmenter, School Management System, GCC Compiler.
questions.a: Ubuntu → SS (OS), MS Word → AS (general purpose), Printer Driver → SS (device driver), Photoshop → AS (general purpose), Python Interpreter → PT (programming tool), Disk Defragmenter → SS (system utility), School Management System → AS (customised), GCC Compiler → PT (programming tool). A wrong classification (e.g., "Python Interpreter is system software") reveals the student cannot distinguish the third category (programming tools) and conflates "software that runs code" with "software that manages hardware."

questions.q: Compare system utilities and device drivers. Both are system software, but they differ in scope and function. Explain the difference with one example of each.
questions.a: System utilities perform maintenance/configuration tasks for the overall system (e.g., Disk Defragmenter reorganizes fragmented files on HDD to improve access speed). Device drivers manage a specific hardware device, acting as a translator between the OS and that device (e.g., GPU driver converts OS draw commands into GPU-specific instructions). The difference: utilities are system-wide maintenance tools; drivers are device-specific interface modules. A wrong answer (e.g., "both do the same thing") reveals the student memorizes categories without understanding functional granularity within system software.

questions.q: A small bakery wants to computerize billing and inventory. The owner asks: "Should I buy Tally (general purpose accounting software) or hire a developer to build custom software?" Evaluate both options using three criteria: cost, fit-to-requirements, and maintenance. Which would you recommend and why?
questions.a: Recommendation: Start with Tally (general purpose). Reasoning: (1) Cost: Tally ~₹18,000/year vs custom development ₹1-3 lakh upfront; (2) Fit: Tally covers 80-90% of standard bakery needs (GST billing, stock, ledgers); custom fits 100% but requires precise requirement gathering; (3) Maintenance: Tally updates automatically for tax changes; custom needs paid developer for every change. For a small bakery with standard needs, Tally's lower cost and zero maintenance burden outweigh perfect fit. A wrong answer (e.g., "always choose custom because it's better") reveals the student cannot evaluate trade-offs and thinks "customised = superior" without considering total cost of ownership.

questions.q: Create a real-world scenario (Indian context) where the same software package could be considered system software in one context and application software in another. Explain the reasoning for each classification.
questions.a: Scenario: "Android OS on a smartphone" vs "Android OS running as a virtual machine on a Windows laptop for app testing." On the smartphone, Android is system software — it directly manages hardware (cellular radio, touchscreen, sensors) and provides the platform for all apps. On the Windows laptop, the Android VM is an application software — it runs as a user-level process on top of Windows, performing the user task "test mobile apps" without managing the laptop's physical hardware. The classification depends on whether the software directly controls physical hardware (system) or runs as a user task on another OS (application). A poor answer (e.g., "it's always system software") reveals rigid categorization without understanding the relational nature of the classification.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: System software is a collection of programs that directly manages and controls computer hardware resources (CPU, memory, devices) and provides a platform for running other software, while application software is designed to perform specific user-oriented tasks (document creation, ______, media playback) by utilizing the services provided by system software.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you press the power button on your laptop — the screen shows a logo, then a login screen ______, and only after you log in can you open Chrome or MS Word.
What is System software? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: System software is a collection of programs that directly manages and controls computer hardware resources (CPU, memory, devices) and provides a platform for running other software, while application software is designed to perform specific user-oriented tasks (document creation, calculations, media playback) by utilizing the services.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about System software?
questions.a: Students believe "System Software = Operating System only" and forget system utilities (disk cleanup, antivirus, backup tools) and device drivers (printer, graphics, USB drivers).

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Student can classify any given software as system software, application software, or programming tool with justification, explain the dependency relationship (system software must load before application software), and provide three distinct examples of each category with their specific functions in a computer system.
